newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hero's widow says she saw husband die on TV.
newsitem.headline: Peru hero's widow says she saw husband die on TV.

text.p: The widow of a Peruvian commando said on Friday she watched her husband dying on live television as he was taken on a stretcher from the Japanese ambassador's home after he rescued hostages from rebels in a bloody raid.
But Marina Collado said she only realised her husband, army Lt. Col. Juan Valer, took part in the raid that freed all but one of 72 hostages when the images appeared on her televison screen at work.
"I was in my office working with my colleagues. I recognised him even with paint on his face," Collado told local television station America.

A composed Collado, who wept openly on Thursday at a huge public burial for her husband, Peru's latest hero, said that when she saw Valer, "my colleagues told me 'It's not him,' but I could feel it was."
Her husband died from seven bullet wounds received as he led the rebels' prize captive, Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, to safety.
One hostage, two commandos and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels died in the assault launched from tunnels underneath the diplomatic residence.
